subject: pe
title: Practical Performance
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Practical Performance in GCSE PE.
meta_desc: GCSE PE adventure on Practical Performance.
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Practical Performance.

concepts.def: A skill performed in an unpredictable environment constantly affected by surroundings, such as a pass in football, requiring the performer to adapt.
A self-paced skill performed in a stable, predictable environment not affected by opponents, such as a free throw or a serve.
Continuous practice without rest intervals, best suited to simple, discrete, closed skills and to fit, experienced performers.
Practice broken up with rest or alternative activities, best suited to beginners, complex skills and tasks that are tiring or dangerous.
Information a performer receives about a performance; it can be intrinsic (felt internally) or extrinsic (from others), and positive or negative.
Targets that are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic and Time-bound, used to structure improvement and maintain motivation in practical performance.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Practical Performance — a core area of GCSE PE.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Practical Performance brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Practical Performance.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A tennis serve is best classified as a:
options: Open skill
Closed skill
Gross skill only
Externally paced skill

mcqs.q: Distributed practice is most suitable for:
options: Experienced performers only
Beginners and complex or tiring skills
Simple discrete skills
Fit athletes only
The coach
The performer's own senses
The scoreboard
Teammates

mcqs.q: The 'M' in SMART goals stands for:
options: Motivating
Measurable
Mental
Maximal

mcqs.q: Is a basketball free throw an open or closed skill?
options: No practice is needed for complex skills.
Open, because basketball is fast and unpredictable.
Neither - it is a fine skill only.
Closed - the environment is stable and the shot is self-paced.

mcqs.q: Which practice suits a nervous beginner learning a complex skill?
options: Distributed practice, with rests between attempts.
Extrinsic and intrinsic mean the same thing.
No practice is needed for complex skills.
Massed practice, to do as many reps as possible.

mcqs.q: Does extrinsic feedback come from inside the performer?
options: No - extrinsic feedback comes from external sources like a coach or scoreboard.
No practice is needed for complex skills.
Yes, it is the 'feel' of the movement.
Extrinsic and intrinsic mean the same thing.
